utility.notes: Entergy Louisiana is Baton Rouge's well-established dominant electric utility (distinct from Entergy New Orleans, which serves the separate New Orleans market with its own net-metering rules).

value.name: Entergy Louisiana
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Baton Rouge's residential solar customers this session; Entergy Louisiana is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish operate a consolidated City-Parish government; the Department of Public Works (DPW) Permit & Inspection Division is the single permitting authority for the whole consolidated jurisdiction.

permit_authority.value: City of Baton Rouge / East Baton Rouge Parish, Department of Public Works Permit & Inspection Division
permit_authority.notes: The Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code (LSUCC) is a genuinely mandatory statewide code (adopting the 2021 I-Codes with Louisiana amendments plus the NEC) — no parish or municipality may adopt a more or less stringent code, a uniquely uniform statewide baseline compared to several other states researched this session. Enforcement is local: Baton Rouge/East Baton Rouge Parish's own consolidated DPW Permit & Inspection Division is the AHJ.

interconnection_url.notes: Per Entergy Louisiana's own page: residential net metering covers systems up to 25kW AC. Systems installed by 2019-12-31 are grandfathered at full retail-rate crediting through 2034-12-31. Systems installed after 2019-12-31 use 'two-channel billing' under Rider Schedule DG: the customer pays full retail rate for all grid electricity purchased, while excess exported energy is credited separately at a fixed rate ($0.0259331/kWh, effective 2025-04-01) rather than at the retail rate — a materially lower-value structure than legacy net metering. Monthly bills cannot drop below the fixed Customer Charge; excess credits carry forward. These rules do not apply to Entergy New Orleans customers, who fall under a separate program.

battery_programs.notes: The City's own permit information sheet notes that a plot plan must show battery locations if used, and references a separate 'battery storage permit' concept in general search context, but no dedicated financial battery incentive program was independently confirmed this session.

value.name: Completed Plan Review application with the plan review fee

Manufacturer documentation showing the mounting/racking system withstands a 105mph wind load, including bolt size, length, and connection spacing to the roof (existing rafters must have purlin bracing installed if not already present)
Plot plan showing the location of solar panels, disconnect(s), inverter, electric meter(s), and batteries (if used)
Electrical plan (riser diagram) showing system wiring/connection to the building's electrical system, including wire size/type, grounding, overcurrent protection rating, and disconnects
Manufacturer specifications for the solar panel and inverter, including ratings and overcurrent protection

Plumbing plan including pipe size/type, exchange tank location, backup water heater, pump, and whether the heat exchanger coil directly contacts potable water; requires separate East Baton Rouge Parish Health Unit approval

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Solar Permit Information' sheet. Solar permits require a Louisiana-licensed electrical contractor and solar contractor. The City/Parish does not enforce private subdivision restrictions — applicants must separately obtain HOA/subdivision approval before permitting.

inspection_steps.notes: Not detailed in the City's own information sheet fetched this session. Per broader search context (not independently confirmed from this specific document), the City/Parish offers an Expedited Plan Review option returning residential reviews in about 3 business days via the MyGovernmentOnline (MGO) portal — recorded with lower confidence pending direct primary-source re-confirmation, so not stated in timeline_days below.

timeline_days.notes: No specific review-to-issuance day count was stated in the City's own 'Solar Permit Information' sheet fetched this session.

other_conditions: Electrical and plumbing (water heating) permits are separate from the base solar permit and are additionally required
The 25kW AC figure recorded here reflects the statewide Entergy Louisiana residential net-metering cap, not a separate City/Parish permit-eligibility limit
